investigations.name: ACME Flame Design
investigations.hardware: Advanced Combustion via Microgravity Experiments (ACME), Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR), Reconfiguration of Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR)
investigations.summary: The primary objectives of this flight experiment are: A. Obtain soot-inception limits of quasi-steady normal and inverse spherical diffusion flames as functions of flow rate, Zst, amount of inert (N2 or CO2), and pressure for C2H4 and CH4 flames. Identify the corresponding temperatures in hot regions. Obtain similar limits and temperatures for inverse and normal coflow flames. B. Obtain detailed measurements in quasi-steady normal and inverse spherical diffusion flames for C2H4 and CH4. Determine the effects of flow rate, Zst, amount of N2, and pressure on flame temperature, size, color, and soot volume fraction. Evaluate the possible existence of steady flames. C. Obtain extinction limits…
investigations.blurb: Gaseous ethylene flames in the ACME hardware, used to study normal and inverse flame structure rather than a spacecraft material.
investigations.oxygenNote: The inverse-flame table reaches 85% oxygen. The challenge names CFI-G as the high-oxygen microgravity series. Flame Design is flame structure, not the habitat or suit screen.

relevance.iss: Maps how a gaseous flame sits in the CIR, which is context for material tests but not a flammability limit for cabin fabrics.
relevance.moon: Inverse flames change where the oxygen is, a useful bound when habitat oxygen is enriched, but the fuel is ethylene gas.
relevance.suit: Not a spacesuit-atmosphere materials test. Oxygen in these runs is a flame-structure variable.
relevance.earth: Fundamental gaseous-flame structure, weak link to terrestrial firefighting gear.

investigations.name: ACME Burning Rate Emulator
investigations.summary: The BRE flight program seeks to establish the burning conditions in a quiescent microgravity ambient in terms of material properties. The specific flight objectives are as follows. 1. Observe burning behavior in long-duration microgravity for CH4/N2 and C2H4/N2mixtures on porous circular burners of 25 and 50 mm diameter. Consider O2/N2 ambients with various pressures and ambient O2 concentrations and pressures. NASA - considered atmosphere for human space missions will be examined: 14.7 psia, 21 % oxygen: 10.2 psia, 26.5 %; and 8.2 psia, 34 % oxygen. Emphasize fuel conditions that can be related to a diverse range of condensed fuels. 2. Consider the conditions of Objective 1 for ambients…
investigations.blurb: Burning Rate Emulator studied material flammability in a still atmosphere by matching the burning rate of a solid with a gaseous burner.

relevance.iss: Still-atmosphere flammability is the no-ventilation limit inside a rack or a closed volume on station.
relevance.moon: Oxygen was varied from about 21 percent up through the mid-30s and 40 percent, the range expected in a lunar habitat.
relevance.suit: The high-oxygen BRE points are the closest still-air screen to a suit atmosphere short of the CFI-G burner.
relevance.earth: A method for screening materials without a large fire, not a detector or turnout-gear result.

investigations.name: ACME Coflow Laminar Diffusion Flame
investigations.summary: In order to provide the experimental data needed to allow rigorous testing of computational models at the extremes of the fuel dilution spectrum, we have the following objectives: A) Characterize the behavior of weak coflow diffusion flames of methane and ethylene, as a function of velocity and fuel dilution, through measurement of flame shape, lift-off heights, temperatures and extinction limits. B) Characterize the sooting tendencies of diffusion flames with long residence times, as a function of velocity and fuel dilution, through measurement of flame shape, gas temperatures in the soot-free portion of the flame, soot luminosity, soot temperatures, and soot volume fractions.
investigations.blurb: Coflow laminar diffusion flames of gaseous fuel in ACME. Supporting combustion science, not a solid-material flammability test.

relevance.iss: Shows how a laminar jet flame behaves without buoyancy. Indirect for cabin material selection.
relevance.moon: Coflow speed is a stand-in for ventilation, but the fuel is gas, not habitat plastic or fabric.
relevance.suit: Does not address 100 percent oxygen at suit pressure.
relevance.earth: Laboratory flame structure, not firefighter equipment.

investigations.name: ACME E-FIELD Flames
investigations.summary: The objective of this investigation is to better understand the relationship between electric field voltage and chemi-ion current, analyze the dynamic response of flames to electric field changes, evaluate soot formation, and characterize stabilized near-limit lifted flames.
investigations.blurb: Electric-field effects on laminar diffusion flames. PSI has no partial-gravity combustion data yet; this experiment used the electric field on flame ions to mimic a body force.

relevance.iss: A gaseous-flame body-force study. Secondary to BASS and SAME for station operations.
relevance.moon: The Moon is partial gravity. Until LUCI and FM2 fly, E-FIELD is the PSI stand-in that puts a force on the flame.
relevance.suit: Does not reproduce suit oxygen concentration.
relevance.earth: Ion-driven flow is a research tool, not a fire-service product.

relevance.iss: Explains why a station flame is spherical and diffusion-limited once buoyancy is gone.
relevance.moon: Spherical flames are the zero-g end of the bound. Lunar gravity sits between this and a normal flame.
relevance.suit: Shape study, not a suit-material limit.
relevance.earth: The contrast with a teardrop flame is teaching material, not a product.

relevance.iss: Directly the materials and the low-speed ventilation a crew cabin actually has.
relevance.moon: Solid fuels (films, fabrics) plus a measured oxygen level are what a lunar habitat material screen needs.
relevance.suit: Shows how the same solids behave as oxygen rises, which is the direction a suit prebreathe and cabin move.
relevance.earth: Suppression and spread on thin materials informs how fabrics burn, loosely related to turnout gear.

investigations.blurb: Burning and Suppression of Solids. Bridged the NASA-STD-6001 ground test and real microgravity flammability, and tried a gaseous extinguisher like the ISS agent.

relevance.iss: SIBAL fabric and PMMA in the glovebox duct, plus a nitrogen-style extinguisher already used on station.
relevance.moon: Thicker, realistic solids in a forced flow. Habitat oxygen will be higher than these early runs, so read them as the low-oxygen bound.

investigations.name: Cool Flames Investigation
investigations.hardware: Multi-User Droplet Combustion Apparatus (MDCA), Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR)
investigations.summary: The objectives of this investigation are to: 1) Examine the combustion behavior of n-dodecane and mixtures of n-dodecane/iso-dodecane at pressures ranging from 0.25 atm to 5 atm. 2) Analyze the effects of helium dilution on cool flame behavior. 3) Examine the behavior of combustion characteristics. 4) Investigate the relationship between droplet size, pressure, and flame extinction, and (5) understand the consequence of soot formation during cool flame combustion.
investigations.blurb: Cool flames around liquid-fuel droplets. A flame can look out and still be burning in a cool-flame mode, which matters for declaring a fire extinguished.

relevance.iss: Droplet fuels in cabin atmospheres. Cool-flame survival means a visible extinction is not always the end of combustion.
relevance.moon: Oxygen and diluent were varied. Cool flames are a suppression false-negative, not a materials limit.
relevance.earth: Explains reignition after an apparent extinguishment. Indirect for terrestrial nozzles.

investigations.summary: The focus of DAFT / DAFT-2 was to mitigate the risk for the Smoke Aerosol Measurement Experiment (SAME). SAME relied on a commercially available condensate nuclei counter, the TSI P-Trak, to quantify smoke aerosols in a microgravity environment, however there were concerns that th P-Trak would not be reliable in microgravity as it relies on gravity to recycle isopropyl alcohol used in the measurement process. DAFT / DAFT-2 tests that a modified P-Trak particulate counter would be accurate in microgravity. Summarized objectives include: 1) Demonstrate the Functionality of the Modified TSI P-Trak in Microgravity 2) Compare the TSI P-Trak Performance against the DustTrak control 3) Create and…

investigations.name: SPICE data analysis
investigations.family: Analysis or model, not a new burn
investigations.summary: This ground investigation sought to increase understanding of the issues that control the large discrepancy between soot formation in 1g and in 0g flames. The objective of this investigation was to integrate computational and experimental methods to derive temperature distributions and soot volume fractions from the Smoke Point in Coflow Experiment (SPICE) data available in PSI. By analyzing over 1600 raw DSLR images and incorporating advanced soot models, the study sought to improve understanding of soot formation, oxidation, radiative re-absorption, and aggregate growth in heavily sooting flames. The work further aimed to reconcile microgravity and normal gravity flame behavior, identify…

relevance.iss: Soot-point models support how much smoke a detector might see. Secondary to SAME itself.
relevance.moon: No habitat oxygen or dust measurement.
relevance.earth: Soot modeling only.

investigations.name: Concurrent flame spread vs BASS
investigations.family: Analysis or model, not a new burn
investigations.summary: The objective of this research was to develop and validate new flamelet generated manifold (FGM) modeling techniques for concurrent flame spread in microgravity. Concurrent flame spread presented one of the greatest modeling challenges in combustion science due to the intricate coupling between heat transfer, mass transport, and chemical kinetics near the solid-vapor interface. Traditional modeling strategies often relied on hybridized turbulence and chemistry models that were not fully consistent and failed to capture important intermediate reaction pathways. To overcome these shortcomings, this PSI grant advanced the use of an unsteady flamelet generated manifold (UFGM) framework that…
investigations.blurb: Concurrent flame-spread modeling with flamelet-generated manifolds, checked against BASS. A model, not a new burn.

relevance.iss: A way to extrapolate BASS spread instead of burning every material on station.
relevance.moon: The model is only as good as the BASS oxygen range it was checked against.
relevance.earth: Numerical method, not hardware.

relevance.moon: Oxygen mole fractions in the test matrix reach about 0.30, which touches the lunar-habitat band.

The mission seeks to validate and improve simplified models by incorporating detailed chemical reactions, heat transfer, and material movement, using both space-based data and extensive ground-based tests. Key flight experiment goals include obtaining high-resolution measurements of droplet burning rates, flame extinction behavior, heat radiation, soot levels, and…

investigations.name: Saffire-I
investigations.family: Cygnus vehicle after it left the ISS
investigations.summary: The objectives of this investigation were to: (1) determine how rapidly a large scale fire grows in low-gravity and (2) investigate the low-g flammability limits compared to those obtained in NASA’s normal gravity material flammability screening test.
investigations.blurb: First large-scale spacecraft fire. A cotton-fiberglass blend about a meter long, burned in Cygnus after it left the station.

relevance.iss: The first burn bigger than an index card in a real spacecraft volume, at cabin oxygen near 21 percent and a set airflow.
relevance.moon: Scale is right for a habitat. Oxygen in Saffire-I is still the station value, so it is the low-oxygen large-fire bound.
relevance.suit: Too big and too lean to be a suit fire. It bounds the vehicle the suit returns to.
relevance.earth: Large-sample spread in a confined volume is a research result, not a ground product.

investigations.name: Saffire-II

investigations.name: Cool-flame counterflow
investigations.family: Analysis or model, not a new burn
investigations.summary: By using the Flame Extinguishment (FLEX) experimental data from the Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) system of combustion science, the purpose of this grant was to conduct new simulations and ground-based experiments using ozone-sensitized counterflow flames to: 1) Develop a new diagram of the flammability limits of diffusional cool flames affected by radiation, diffusion, and convection. 2) Bridge the knowledge gap between the flammability limits and extinction limits of hot flames and cool flames. 3) Verify the phenomena observed on the ISS flame extinguishment experiments. 4) Obtain new, quantitative data of extinction limit, flame temperature, and species distribution for the…
investigations.blurb: Quantitative studies of cool-flame transitions at radiation and stretch extinction in counterflow. A data index more than a flight matrix.

relevance.iss: Stretch and radiation extinction bound when a cool flame dies. Secondary to FLEX.
relevance.moon: No habitat oxygen series in the table we hold.
relevance.earth: Counterflow extinction is a lab method.

investigations.name: ACME CFI-G
investigations.summary: 1. Plan and support flight testing on the International Space Station (ISS). 2. Determine the conditions for which cool diffusion flames occur for propane, n-butane, and n-pentane; normal and inverse flames; and a broad range of Zst, Tad, and fluent flow rate. 3. Support the flight tests with advanced CFD simulations. 4. Identify or develop a chemical kinetics mechanism that yields good agreement between the CFD predictions and the ISS measurements. 5. Disseminate the results as widely as possible.
investigations.blurb: Cool Flames Investigation with Gases. An oxygen-nitrogen mixture, up to about 85 percent oxygen, flows from the spherical burner into a fuel-nitrogen chamber. The highest-oxygen microgravity tests in this set.
investigations.oxygenNote: CFI-G flows an oxygen-nitrogen mixture from a spherical burner into a fuel-nitrogen chamber, an inside-out flame, up to about 85% oxygen.

relevance.iss: Most station air is 21 percent oxygen. CFI-G is the enriched-oxygen extreme, not the daily cabin.
relevance.moon: A lunar habitat is expected at 30 percent oxygen or more, at 10.2 psi or less. CFI-G is the only PSI series that reaches well above that, up to about 85 percent.
relevance.suit: A suit is 100 percent oxygen at 4.3 psi. CFI-G does not hit 4.3 psi, but it is the high-oxygen flame data that bounds suit fire behavior.
relevance.earth: High-oxygen burner flames are not a ground fire-service dataset.

context.label: Apollo 1
context.summary: In 1967 a fire in a pure-oxygen cabin during a pre-launch test killed the Apollo 1 crew.

context.label: Apollo 13
context.summary: An oxygen-tank explosion on the way to the Moon disabled the service module.

context.label: Mir oxygen-generator fire
